selected_articles.title: Rolls-Royce wins Delta Air Lines order for 30 Trent XWB-84 EP and 32 Trent 7000 engines
key_facts: Delta Air Lines orders 30 Trent XWB-84 EP engines and 32 Trent 7000 engines
Engines will power 15 Airbus A350-900s and 16 Airbus A330neo aircraft
Fleet to be covered by Rolls-Royce TotalCare service
Delta is described as Rolls-Royce's largest partner in the Americas
selected_articles.summary: Rolls-Royce announces Delta Air Lines has placed an order for 30 Trent XWB-84 EP engines and 32 Trent 7000 engines to power 15 A350-900s and 16 A330neos, with TotalCare coverage for the fleet. The carrier is highlighted as RR's largest partner in the Americas, reinforcing RR’s propulsion footprint in North American widebody fleets.

selected_articles.title: Rolls-Royce signs TotalCare agreements with China Airlines for 36 Trent XWB engines
key_facts: China Airlines signs TotalCare for 36 Trent XWB engines (30 XWB-97 and 6 XWB-84)
Engines will power 15 Airbus A350-1000 and 3 A350-900 aircraft
Fleet will reach 33 A350s after deliveries
TotalCare coverage extended to the China Airlines fleet
selected_articles.summary: China Airlines has signed TotalCare for 36 Trent XWB engines, comprising 30 XWB-97 and 6 XWB-84, to power 15 A350-1000s and 3 A350-900s, with the fleet ultimately totaling 33 A350s and continued RR service support.

selected_articles.title: Rolls-Royce welcomes EGYPTAIR’s order for an additional 12 Trent XWB-84 engines that will power six Airbus A350-900
key_facts: EgyptAir orders 12 Trent XWB-84 engines
Engines power six Airbus A350-900s
TotalCare service agreement for the fleet signed at Paris Airshow 2025
First aircraft due to enter service later this year
selected_articles.summary: EgyptAir has placed an order for 12 Trent XWB-84 engines to power six A350-900s, with a fleet TotalCare service agreement signed for the Future fleet; first A350-900 to enter service later this year.

selected_articles.title: Rolls-Royce Marks a Milestone Ahead of Defense Show, with Saudis Representing over 80% of its Workforce
key_facts: World Defense Show (WDS) 2026 in Riyadh scheduled for 8–12 February 2026
Saudi nationals represent over 80% of RR’s workforce in the Kingdom
MEPC authorised MRO, MAKEEN local power solutions, Salam agreement with RSAF
Riyadh Air MoU to purchase 100 Trent XWB-97 engines for up to 50 A350-1000s
selected_articles.summary: Rolls-Royce highlights its Saudi localization and sovereign capability drive ahead of WDS 2026, noting Saudi nationals exceed 80% of its local workforce, the MEPC/MRO framework, and a Saudi orders push including a MoU for 100 Trent XWB-97 engines to power up to 50 A350-1000s.

selected_articles.title: Rolls-Royce Holdings Plc 2025 Full Year Results
key_facts: Underlying operating profit £3.5bn; margin 17.3%
Revenue £20,059m (underlying) / £21,207m (statutory); free cash flow £3.3bn
Net cash £1.895bn at 31 December 2025
2026 guidance: underlying profit £4.0–£4.2bn; free cash flow £3.6–£3.8bn
Announced £7–£9bn multi-year share buyback for 2026–2028 (with £2.5bn in 2026)
selected_articles.summary: Rolls-Royce reports 2025 full-year results with underlying operating profit of £3.5bn and 17.3% margin, revenue of £20.059bn underlying, free cash flow £3.3bn, and a strong balance sheet, guiding to £4.0–£4.2bn in 2026 and announcing a £7–£9bn buyback for 2026–2028.

selected_articles.title: The next evolution of aviation
key_facts: UltraFan technologies aim to power future widebody/narrowbody propulsion
UltraFan programme targets fuel efficiency, durability, reduced noise and emissions
UltraFan is SAF-ready from day one and designed for compatibility with alternative fuels and hydrogen
selected_articles.summary: Rolls-Royce outlines the UltraFan technology programme as a path to the next generation of widebody/narrowbody propulsion, focusing on fuel efficiency, durability, noise and emissions reductions, with SAF/hydrogen compatibility and immediate SAF readiness.

selected_articles.title: GE Aerospace and Safran CFM Partnership
key_facts: CFM International established in 1974 as 50/50 venture between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines
CFM56: powering 14,650+ aircraft; 54,000+ engines ordered; 42,500+ delivered
LEAP: powering ~3,500 aircraft; 8-year in-service fleet maturity; 20%+ fuel savings target via RISE
RISE program aims for sustainable engine tech with reduced fuel burn and emissions
selected_articles.summary: GE Aerospace and Safran mark 50 years of the CFM partnership, highlighting massive engine fleet milestones (CFM56/LEAP), and the RISE program aimed at more than 20% reductions in fuel burn and CO2 emissions for future engines.

selected_articles.title: GE Aviation and Safran Launch Advanced Technology Demonstration Program for Sustainable Engines; Extend CFM Partnership to 2050
key_facts: CFM RISE program targets >20% lower fuel consumption/CO2 vs today
Open fan architecture, hybrid electric capability; demonstrator tests mid-2020s
100% SAF and hydrogen capability in scope; partnership extended to 2050
selected_articles.summary: GE Aviation and Safran kick off the CFM RISE technology demonstration to achieve more than 20% lower fuel consumption and CO2, include open fan architecture and hybrid electric concepts, with SAF/hydrogen readiness and a partnership extension through 2050.

selected_articles.title: GE Aerospace $1bn investment to boost Leap engine production
key_facts: GE to invest $1 billion to accelerate LEAP engine production
Aims to strengthen supply chain and support around-the-world customers
selected_articles.summary: GE Aerospace commits about $1 billion to accelerate LEAP engine production, signaling ongoing competitive pressure in next-generation narrowbody propulsion markets.

selected_articles.title: DAP 2026: India's new defence procurement policy aims for indigenous tech sovereignty
key_facts: MoD proposed DAP 2026 to accelerate capital acquisitions and strengthen domestic capability
Co-develop and own IP for procured defence products; emphasis on domestic design and manufacturing
Faster procurement processes and increased use of modern technologies
selected_articles.summary: India's Defence Acquisition Procedure 2026 draft aims to accelerate indigenous tech development and give domestic firms IP rights, potentially reshaping global supplier dynamics and opportunities for defence exports.

selected_articles.title: Special Report: India reforms defence procurement procedure
key_facts: India moving to co-develop and own IP for procured equipment
Focus on indigenous design, manufacturing readiness and faster trials
Spiral designing and staged procurements to evaluate modern tech
selected_articles.summary: Janes reports on India’s defence procurement reforms, highlighting IP ownership, domestic design focus, and accelerated procurement processes that could influence global defence supply chains.

selected_articles.title: India's Defence Leap From Indigenous Production to Global Exports, Redefining National Security
key_facts: Defence budget rising from ₹2.53 lakh crore (2013-14) to ₹6.81 lakh crore (2025-26)
193 contracts worth ₹2,09,050 crore signed in 2024-25; 177 domestic
Defence exports ₹23,622 crore in FY 2024-25
Defence Industrial Corridors in UP and Tamil Nadu; 253 MoUs; investments ₹8,658 crore
selected_articles.summary: India’s defence trajectory shows record production and exports with a multi-hundred-billion-rupee budget, domestic manufacturing emphasis, and defence corridors, signaling meaningful upside for indigenous suppliers and potential export growth.
